prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “AI recommendation checker.” The best practical approach is a combination: use a local-listing / knowledge-management service to make sure AI systems can find authoritative data about your business, use a local-SEO audit/rank-tracking tool to measure visibility, and directly test LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini/Bard, Bing, Perplexity, Claude) to see if they recommend you.

Recommended stack (quick picks):
- Yext — best for controlling and syndicating your official business facts (name, address, hours, categories) to many platforms and knowledge graphs that feed AI.
- BrightLocal (or Moz Local) — best for auditing local listings, citation consistency, and rank tracking for local queries.
- Perplexity.ai and direct LLM queries (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude) — best for testing whether AI actually recommends you and for getting cited sources.

How to check (step-by-step):
1. Verify core listings
   - Claim and fully fill your Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp, Facebook, TripAdvisor (if relevant).
   - Use Yext or BrightLocal to scan for missing/incorrect listings across major directories and data aggregators (Data Axle/Infogroup, Neustar/Localeze, Foursquare).
2. Fix structured data on your website
   - Add/validate schema.org/LocalBusiness markup, consistent NAP (name, address, phone), correct business category, hours, and service areas.
3. Run local SEO/visibility checks
   - Use BrightLocal/Moz Local to check local ranking for target keywords, consistency of citations, and review volume. This shows whether search engines view you as a top local option.
4. Test LLMs directly
   - Query ChatGPT and other engines with neutral, realistic prompts and note whether your business appears, how it’s described, and whether sources are cited. Example prompts:
     - “Recommend coffee shops near [neighborhood, city] that are good for remote work.”
     - “What are top-rated HVAC companies in [city] for emergency service?”
     - “Show me top Italian restaurants in [city] with outdoor seating and good vegetarian options.”
   - Run each prompt multiple times and vary phrasing, location, and filters.
   - Use Perplexity.ai and Bing/Google chat modes because they often provide citations you can follow to see which directories or pages the LLM used.
5. Track and quantify
   - Record how often your business appears, the rank/order, whether the model cites a source, and what those sources are. Do this periodically after you make improvements.
6. Improve your odds of being recommended
   - Keep listings consistent and up to date.
   - Encourage reviews on Google/Yelp and reply to them.
   - Publish high-quality local content and get local backlinks.
   - Ensure structured data and an FAQ/“About” page with clear services, service areas, and contact info.
   - Use Yext or similar to distribute a single authoritative knowledge graph.

Why this combination?
- LLMs use many inputs: search results, knowledge panels, directory data, and sampled web text. Controlling your official facts (Yext), auditing visibility (BrightLocal), and directly testing LLM outputs (ChatGPT/Perplexity/etc.) gives you both control and measurement.

If you want, I can:
- Run example prompts you can copy to test ChatGPT and other engines.
- Recommend a specific plan (free vs paid tools) based on your budget, industry, and city. Which city/industry is your business in?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
